configuration: gfortran -fdefault-real-8 -O2 -std=legacy (nominal); driver.f, a copy of the upstream test with RANDOM_SEED()/RANDOM_NUMBER() replaced by a fixed ic/ input vector
observable: the sine transform (SINT1F/SINT1B) round-trip max error (both call orders) and the max and mean magnitude of the array produced by the first forward transform of the fixed input, N=1000
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except the input vector is fixed (see the variant note) instead of drawn from the upstream test's unseeded RANDOM_SEED()/RANDOM_NUMBER()
variant: every element of ic/nominal's fixed input vector perturbed by two ulps at binary64 (np.nextafter twice); this is the check's only active initial-condition input, so perturbing all of it is the minimal sufficient perturbation. It moves the transformed array's max and mean magnitude at the 1e-16 to 1e-13 relative level (measured below) on every check; it does not always move the round-trip residual, which is a sum whose exact value is zero and therefore round-off sized regardless of the input (see the pitfall citation in the warrant).
altbuild: the same pinned source built with gfortran -O0 instead of -O2 (same -fdefault-real-8 -std=legacy); FFTPACK's default build is already IEEE (no fast-math), so this is the same-compiler fallback per the NCAR-classic-libraries family ruling, not a strict-IEEE flip

altbuild.what: the same pinned source built with gfortran -O0 instead of -O2 (same -fdefault-real-8 -std=legacy flags); the same-compiler fallback per the NCAR-classic-libraries altbuild family ruling

warrant: roundtrip-max-error compares the |output-input| max over both round-trip call orders on the SAME fixed input; its analytic value is exactly zero, so what is measured is the round-off remainder of the transform's forward and inverse stages (pitfall references/pitfalls/residual-below-one-ulp.md: a residual whose true value is zero carries no information about a port beyond its OK/FAILED verdict against a wide bound). Measured on the worker (x86_64 debian trixie, run1, 2-ulp variant): reference 1.545e-14, candidate 2.445e-14, using 9.000e-06 of the 1e-09 bound (headroom 111,114x). A candidate that does not actually invert the transform (a missing backward call, a wrong routine, a scrambled index map) leaves a round-trip error of order the input itself (about 0.5 to 1 depending on the transform's own scale), 8 to 10 orders of magnitude over the bound: the bound comfortably separates round-off reordering from that fault. transformed-max-magnitude and transformed-mean-magnitude compare the aggregate size of the array the first forward transform produces on the fixed input (sine transform (SINT1F/SINT1B) on a length-1000 vector), so a candidate must actually compute the same transform on the same data, not merely round-trip an unrelated one (tests.json's survey: 'grades the round-trip error and the transformed array'). Because the input is fixed, two correct implementations of the same transform on the same input agree to double-precision round-off under any legitimate reordering (summation order, radix decomposition, compiler, architecture): measured max-magnitude bound_fraction 3.408e-07 (headroom 2,934,312x) and mean-magnitude bound_fraction 1.617e-05 (headroom 61,834x) from the 2-ulp variant, the only calibration evidence available since the altbuild moved nothing on this host (see below). A wrong normalization, a wrong axis, a transposed 2D array, or a transform that never ran moves the magnitude by an order-1 relative amount (or leaves it at the untransformed input's own scale), six to seven orders of magnitude over the 1e-09 bound: the bound leaves real headroom above the measured floor while still separating a plausible fault by a wide margin. altbuild (gfortran -O0 instead of -O2, same -fdefault-real-8 -std=legacy) was measured bit-identical to nominal on this host (distance 0.0, floor 0.0): FFTPACK's fixed-length loop nest gives the same instruction sequence and rounding at either optimisation level here, so it supplies no floor of its own on x86_64. (During authoring, the same altbuild measured natively on macOS arm64 gfortran 15.2 showed the transformed-magnitude agreement at 2e-17 to 8e-16 relative, not zero -- the same fixed source and flags round differently across architectures, matching references/pitfalls/altbuild-floors-are-host-specific.md; the graded record is the x86_64 worker's.) The variant remains the only calibration evidence for this bound, and it already shows several orders of magnitude of headroom below the fault separation above.
